sphere_commentary.overview:
Across all three series the 1-second outcome data show solid efficacy with moderate variance, anchored by 1000 listener responses.
• HEALING carries the largest sample (n=574) and tightest variance, providing the library's most reliable signal layer.
• THRIVING produces the library's top-scoring Hold protocols — T-FC-L3 (mean 7.63) leads the dataset.
• TRANSFORMING carries the widest spread and lowest aggregate mean, consistent with its ascending-arc design.
• YouTube reach remains minimal across all 30 protocols; none exceed 30 cumulative views.
• AutoGluon's predicted scores run materially above observed means in several protocols, flagging latent efficacy not yet realised.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series display efficacy profiles that broadly align with their design intent and arc architecture.
• HEALING Descent protocols cluster tightly around 6.4–7.2 means with consistent std ~1.7, reflecting steady nervous-system regulation.
• THRIVING Hold protocols range 6.5–7.6, with efficacy appearing sensitive to protocol length — longer Holds (L2, L3) trend higher in Focus and Maintenance.
• TRANSFORMING Ascent protocols span 5.7–7.2 with the widest variance, structurally expected for low-affect targeting populations.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
A small number of protocols deviate from series-level expectations and warrant targeted investigation.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean 5.70, std 2.45) — the library's lowest mean and highest variance, possible subgroup effect at L3 depth.
• H-CR-L1 (n=43, mean 6.35) — the lowest mean among HEALING crisis protocols despite larger n; AutoGluon predicts 7.955 for the zone.
• X-ME-L3 (n=18, mean 6.28) — underperforms its L1 and L2 siblings in the same series despite identical arc design intent.
• H-CR-L3 distribution shows immediate-settle mode (7 of 19) alongside several zero responses — a bimodal pattern worth flagging.
• The convergence of low means and high AutoGluon-predicted zone ceilings in crisis and motivation suggests population mismatch rather than protocol failure.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Several concrete protocol development actions emerge from convergent panel observation and AutoGluon divergence.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean 7.63) — create an L2-length variant to test whether Focus gains scale across protocol duration.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean 5.70) — investigate the subgroup; consider an alternative frequency range or extended hold phase.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-OS-L1 (n=95, mean 7.15, 30 YouTube views) — boost discovery via metadata and channel routing; strong efficacy remains under-reached.
• H-CR-L1 (n=43, mean 6.35) — review the L1 vs L2 design delta; AutoGluon's 7.955 crisis-zone ceiling suggests meaningful headroom.
• X-MD-L3 (n=13, mean 7.15, std 2.38) — high mean with high spread; add a midpoint hold segment to stabilise the listener arc.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is widespread and cluster analysis is currently constrained by sparse embeddings.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 29 of 30 protocols show similarity below 0.85, with 12 protocols below 0.65 — analytical framing is actively evolving.
• The most drifted protocols are X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), X-ME-L2 (0.532) — patterns may be genuinely shifting as data grows.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient run history for stable cluster analysis — recompute once embedding volume increases.
• Confidence in embedding-based signal is low for individual protocols but the population-level drift is real and worth tracking.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: This is one of the library's most reliable anxiety protocols — most listeners settle within ten minutes and report noticeable calm. Strong feedback on the rhythm makes it a good everyday choice with room to grow its audience.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Listeners using this mid-length anxiety protocol tend to settle faster than expected, around five minutes, and report steady improvement. It's a quiet, well-balanced option that may be under-reached by its potential audience.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: The longest anxiety descent gives listeners a slower path to calm, with most settling around ten minutes. The rhythm is described as particularly soothing, though the signal is still building.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Designed for moments of acute distress, this protocol shows surprisingly fast settling and meaningful improvement for many listeners. The lower average reflects the wide range of states people arrive in, not a design weakness.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: This mid-length crisis protocol supports steady settling within ten minutes for most listeners, with a few arriving in states the protocol can't yet reach. Listeners and caregivers both report benefit.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: The longest crisis protocol works quickly for some listeners — many feel it within the first minute — while others report little effect. The split reflects the range of crisis states, not the protocol itself.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: For over-stimulated listeners this is the library's most-used protocol, with most settling within ten minutes and reporting noticeable calm. It's the clearest example of strong efficacy waiting to be discovered by more people.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Listeners find this mid-length over-stimulation protocol settles them within about ten minutes, with most reporting meaningful improvement. It's quietly effective and deserves more reach.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: The longest over-stimulation protocol gives a slower path to calm, settling most listeners within ten minutes. The balanced rhythm earns steady approval from those who try it.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: This is a reliable sleep protocol — listeners settle within about five minutes and consistently report improvement. The music earns strong approval, especially from regular users.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Designed for sleep, this mid-length protocol takes a little longer to work for most listeners, around ten to twenty minutes. It's often used by caregivers supporting others, and most report real benefit.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: The longest sleep protocol settles most listeners within ten minutes and earns steady approval for its calm rhythm. It remains one of the quieter corners of the library.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: For creative flow this entry-level protocol often settles listeners within minutes, with music earning strong praise. Responses are broad — some feel a clear creative lift, others find it steady rather than inspiring.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: This mid-length creative-flow protocol tends to work within ten minutes and earns genuine enthusiasm from those who connect with it. The music in particular is loved.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: The longest creative-flow protocol is currently the strongest in its tier, with most listeners reporting clear improvement. The signal is still building but the trend is positive.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: This entry-level focus protocol works for many listeners within five minutes, but feedback on the rhythm is mixed — some find it busier than expected. Results vary with listener state.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: This mid-length focus protocol takes about ten minutes to settle most listeners, who report meaningful improvement. Music feedback is mixed, suggesting the groove style matters more here.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Currently the library's top-performing protocol — most listeners settle within ten minutes and report significant improvement. The rhythm and music both earn strong praise.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: This maintenance protocol takes its time — about twenty minutes for most listeners — but those who settle report meaningful, lasting improvement. It's a slower, steadier option.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: This mid-length maintenance protocol works within ten minutes for most listeners, though feedback is mixed. Some find the rhythm slightly busy, suggesting listener-preference sensitivity.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: The longest maintenance protocol settles most listeners within five minutes and earns steady approval. The picture is still building and the next batch of listeners will sharpen it.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: This entry-level mind-clarity protocol settles most listeners within ten minutes, with the music earning genuine affection. Results are steady and consistent.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: This mid-length mind-clarity protocol settles listeners relatively quickly and earns praise for its calming rhythm. It may be one of TRANSFORMING's under-reached strengths.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: The longest mind-clarity protocol is currently the library's weakest signal — small sample, wide spread, and a few listeners report feeling worse. This is a priority investigation, not a verdict.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: For motivation and drive this entry-level protocol works within ten minutes for most listeners, though some arrive in states it doesn't reach. The signal suggests room to grow.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: This mid-length motivation protocol takes longer to work — around twenty minutes for many listeners — and earns the most mixed feedback in the library. Routing and sequencing may matter here.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: The longest motivation protocol is a paradox — high average score paired with high variance. For some listeners it works powerfully; for others, much less so. Worth watching closely.

by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: This mid-length mood-and-energy protocol takes a little longer to settle most listeners but earns consistent approval from those who connect with it.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: The longest mood-and-energy protocol settles most listeners within ten minutes and reports real improvement for many, though a meaningful share feel no effect. The signal is still developing.
